purpose: make frequently used paths faster by measuring first, caching where it is safe, and proving the gain
entry_criteria: A measured performance problem or objective exists
inputs: hot paths and data access patterns
procedure: Measure the hot path and find where time goes before changing anything.
Fix the cheapest cause first: queries, indexes, repeated work and payload size; add caching only for what remains.
Decide freshness per item: what can be stale, for how long, and what invalidates it.
Design the cache key to include everything that changes the answer, including user or tenant, so one user never sees another's data.
Handle misses and failures: the system must still work correctly when the cache is empty or down.
Measure again under the same conditions and record the gain and the cost (memory, complexity).
acceptance_criteria: The gain is measured under the same conditions as the baseline
Cache keys include tenant or user where data differs
The system is correct with the cache empty or unavailable
validation_method: Performance engineer review of the measurements.

validation.check: run the same load test before and after and compare p95
stop the cache service and run the functional tests

failure_modes.detection: Users see old values past the limit
failure_modes.response: Fix invalidation or shorten the lifetime
Add the tenant to the key and purge; treat as a security incident

worked_example: ILLUSTRATIVE: Profiling shows 70 percent of a product page's time is one repeated query. An index removes most of it; a 60-second cache keyed by product and locale handles the rest, lowering p95 from 900 ms to 240 ms, and the page still works with the cache down.
